scenario: A 38-year-old female with epilepsy presents with active generalized tonic-clonic seizure/status epilepticus after EMS midazolam. The case progresses through benzodiazepine-refractory seizure, phenytoin/Dilantin-associated hypotension, subclinical status, intubation, and refractory status epilepticus requiring ICU/neuro consultation and ongoing management.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's actively seizing, GCS 3 — give lorazepam 4 mg IV now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's still seizing after that first dose — give another lorazepam 4 mg IV now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Still seizing after two doses of lorazepam. Load levetiracetam 1500 mg IV now, and watch her breathing closely - her respiratory rate is down to 7 after those benzos.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Levetiracetam 1500 mg IV going in now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's still seizing with her rate down to 7 and sats only 91% — set up for RSI and intubation now. Start bagging her with the BVM while we get the drugs and tube ready.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's tubed now — get me a post-intubation chest X-ray to confirm tube placement.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's stable on the ventilator now, but I need some history fast. Does she have a history of seizures or epilepsy, and has she missed or run out of any anti-seizure medication recently?

messages.speaker: relative
messages.content: Yes, she has epilepsy. She takes two seizure medicines every day, the topiramate and the Vimpat. I'm not sure if she missed any lately. Is she going to be okay?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: The seizure is controlled now and she's stable on the ventilator — sedated with her breathing supported for us. We're getting a chest X-ray to confirm the breathing tube is in the right position. I can't promise how this will play out yet, and we'll keep monitoring her closely. One thing to know: missing anti-seizure medication is a common trigger for a prolonged seizure like this, so it matters that she stays on her topiramate and Vimpat.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Post-intubation chest X-ray is back. Sats up to 95% on the vent, HR 106, BP 117/73, RR 12.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Post-intubation film looks good — tube's in the right position. Keep her sedated on the current vent settings and keep monitoring her vitals closely.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: One more thing I need quickly — does she have any known drug allergies?

relative_emotion.notes: [clinician: One more thing I need quickly — does she have any known drug allergies?] No emotion changed. messages.speaker: relative
messages.content: Yes, she's allergic to sulfa. Please be careful with that.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Thank you — I've noted the sulfa allergy and I'll flag it in her chart so we avoid it. She's stable on the ventilator right now, sedated with her breathing supported, and we're monitoring her closely.
